text:
customer_john: Hey @sara_support, seeing a pattern where our mobile users on aggressive battery saver (Pixel 6, Android 13) get a stream that just... freezes mid-response. client never gets a final event, no error, connection stays open until app wakes up.

sara_support: Ugh. Can you share a request_id and a short repro? Is it SSE via EventSource or the SDK?

customer_john: Using our native wrapper -> fetch-based SSE polyfill. request_id=rid_20260315_83a9, happened ~10:22AM PST. Attaching trimmed client logs: 
```
[10:22:17] open eventsource /v1/stream rid_20260315_83a9
[10:22:20] recv chunk: {"delta":"Hello"}
[10:22:22] stalled, no socket error, keepalive timers not firing
[10:28:05] app enters battery-saver; socket stuck in ESTABLISHED, no data for 5m
[10:33:25] app wakes, resumes, next chunk arrives
```
No server close codes, server logs show normal token emission then silence.

sara_support: Thanks. Looping in @devin_eng and @jen_sre to check server side & NAT behavior. cc @billing-bot (customer asked if they get billed for partial responses).

devin_eng: Looking at rid_20260315_83a9 — server sent tokens until 10:22:22 then kept writing but the TCP ack window stopped. Upstream shows repeated retransmits, then nothing. Likely client/device paused network stack (doze) while keeping socket open. Can you confirm if device switches network interfaces or disables Wi‑Fi radio when entering saver?

customer_john: It disables Wi‑Fi radio and goes into low-power network mode. App still has permission to keep sockets, but OS drops background network. Happens only when screen off and long idle.

jen_sre: This reads like NAT/firewall rebind + device-level radio freeze. Two problems: (1) TCP connection appears ESTABLISHED on client but NAT mapping expired; server sends data -> unacked -> retransmit -> eventually gives up but our keepalive window is long. (2) Client never gets ECONNRESET because OS queues socket state. Mitigation options: shorter server-side idle detection, explicit SSE heartbeats, or recommend customers to use websocket (mobile tends to keep those alive better) or a periodic user-space heartbeat to re-establish.

chris_mobile: For native Android, battery-saver aggressively prevents background network. Short-term workaround: schedule a periodic WorkManager job every 15s to punch a tiny HTTP HEAD/heartbeat while app is background-allowed (if policy permits). Example (very small):
```
// pseudo
fetch('/heartbeat', {method: 'POST', headers:{'x-client-id':id}})
```
This forces network to wake and keep NAT binding. Not ideal but helps.

customer_john: Ok we'll try the heartbeat. Any server-side config we can change so we don't keep charging users for partial tokens? We got a billing complaint.

billing-bot: automatic note: When a stream has no final event and is interrupted by client network drop, usage is prorated to last emitted token. If you want a manual review, open billing ticket with the request_id.

devin_eng: On the infra side we can lower our aggressive retransmit timeout for connections flagged as mobile-ish or route through smarter edge proxies that detect zero acks and fast-fail after 30s of no ack. That avoids long server-sends that never reach the client. I'll prototype a short-circuit for mobile IPs.

sara_support: Action items: 1) @customer_john try heartbeat work-around and confirm. 2) @devin_eng and @jen_sre investigate server fast-fail for NAT-rebinds (devin taking). 3) billing: manual review if customer opens ticket with rid_20260315_83a9.

customer_john: Thanks all — I'll roll heartbeat to a small percent of users and report back. Appreciate quick triage. :pray:

devin_eng: Note for logs — if you see many "sndbuf full / retransmit timeout" entries from our edge for a given IP, tag them as NAT-rebind candidates. Adding that to our detection heuristics. :eyes:

jen_sre: Also recommend enabling SSE comment-style heartbeat on server: send ":\n\n" every 15s. That helps some middleboxes. We'll add a flag in the routing layer to enable it per-route.

customer_john: Great — will test both. If we still see partial outputs after that we'll open a support ticket with traces.

sara_support: Perfect — thx everyone. Keeping thread open until customer confirms.
